 76ers navigating lineup challenges ahead of visit to Magic
 Nov 18, 2026 | 10:00 AM 
 The Philadelphia 76ers have been successful this season, even with their rendition of musical chairs.
 The 76ers likely will continue to shuffle stars in and out of the lineup on Wednesday when they look to extend their three-game winning streak against the host Orlando Magic.
 Joel Embiid recorded 37 points and Jaylen Brown added 31 for the second straight day to go along with 13 rebounds in Philadelphia’s 135-123 victory over the Brooklyn Nets on Monday.
 “We scaled back a little bit and coming out of games, especially the last six games, I feel fresh,” Embiid said. “The next day usually I feel it a little bit and then it’s a recovery day and then you get up one morning, it takes a little bit longer than usual. But the last, probably two weeks, it feels like normal. It feels like I could play a back-to-back. So that’s a good feeling.”
 Embiid sat out Sunday’s victory over the Indiana Pacers and was questionable for Monday’s contest due to right foot plantar fascia injury management.
 Whether Brown sits out on Wednesday is up in the air. He received some battle scars after bonking heads with Brooklyn’s Julius Randle and later tweaking his left hamstring.
 “My head is OK, and the hamstring, it’s a little tight,” Brown said. “Maybe take a look at it (Tuesday) and see how it feels and go from there.”
 The 76ers played without superstar LeBron James (lower back/sciatica management) on Monday.
 Musical chairs aside, the 76ers have won 12 of their first 15 games to start the season. It’s their best start to a campaign over a 15-game stretch since the 2000-01 team won 13 of their first 15 contests. That club lost to the Los Angeles Lakers in the NBA Finals.
 The Magic extended their season-high win streak to four games with a 115-105 victory over the Boston Celtics on Monday.
 Desmond Bane collected 24 points and eight rebounds, while Franz Wagner added 21 points, eight rebounds and nine assists. Wagner has scored at least 20 points in five straight games and nine times this season.
 “We did a great job of attacking (and) did a great job of handling their pressure at the end,” Orlando head coach Sean Sweeney said after the win. “I thought our competitiveness and our effort on both ends was phenomenal.”
 Jalen Suggs celebrated his return to the starting lineup with 12 points, six rebounds and four assists.
 “That was a J. Suggs game right there,” Bane said. “Offensive rebounds, blocking shots, getting in the paint, knocked down a couple big 3s. That’s him. He’s a winning player. You can plug him in with any lineup and he’s going to find a way to impact winning. I thought he did that at a really high level tonight.”
 The 76ers won two of the three meetings last season against the Magic, including the lone encounter in Orlando. Tyrese Maxey had 29 points and three steals and Embiid added 22 points and nine rebounds in Philadelphia’s 103-91 victory over the host Magic on Jan. 9.
